items.question: How long does NDIS registration take?
items.answer: Timeframes depend on your registration scope, audit pathway, documentation readiness and auditor availability. We help you complete the documentation, coaching and audit readiness steps as efficiently as possible.

items.question: Do I need to be a registered NDIS provider?
items.answer: Yes, if you support NDIA-managed participants or deliver higher-risk supports. We can assess your situation in a free consultation and advise on the best way forward.

items.question: What is included in the NDIS policy pack?
items.answer: More than 40 documents covering complaints management, incident reporting, privacy, service agreements, risk registers and more, all tailored to your registration groups.

items.question: How does Easy Compliance work?
items.answer: Easy Compliance is our integrated compliance support platform. We configure it for your operations, import your documents, train your team and provide AI-assisted validation to keep you audit-ready.

items.question: How much does Easy Compliance onboarding cost?
items.answer: Onboarding costs depend on the size and complexity of your organisation. Book a free consultation for a transparent, no-obligation quote.

items.question: Can I get help with just one service?
items.answer: Yes. Our services are modular, so you choose exactly what you need, whether that is NDIS registration, bookkeeping, payroll, compliance or something else.

items.question: Do you only work with established businesses?
items.answer: We work with startups and established businesses alike, with flexible support from initial company registration through to scaling operations.

items.question: How are your consulting services delivered?

page_sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions About the Training
page_sections.intro: Everything you need to know before you enrol, from curriculum structure to delivery formats and certificates.

items.question: Who is this training designed for?
items.answer: The curriculum is designed for Support Coordinators, Specialist Support Coordinators, NDIS providers onboarding new staff and RTOs that need a comprehensive, audit-ready training package. It also suits plan managers and allied health professionals who work alongside Support Coordinators.

items.question: What are the 12 modules and how long does each take?
items.answer: The 12 modules cover: (1) Introduction to the NDIS, (2) Role & Responsibilities of a Support Coordinator, (3) NDIS Practice Standards & Code of Conduct, (4) Plan Implementation & Budget Management, (5) Goal Setting & Participant-Centred Practice, (6) Stakeholder & Provider Coordination, (7) Documentation & Reporting Requirements, (8) Risk Management & Incident Response, (9) Complex Needs & Specialist Support Coordination, (10) Cultural Safety & Diversity, (11) Workforce Development & Self-Care, and (12) Audit Readiness & Continuous Improvement. Each module is designed for approximately 2–3 hours of self-paced learning, totalling 24–36 hours across the full curriculum.

items.question: Is the curriculum aligned with the NDIS Practice Standards?
items.answer: Yes. Every module is mapped to the NDIS Practice Standards and the NDIS Code of Conduct, and the curriculum references NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission requirements, so it suits providers preparing for verification or certification audits.

items.question: Do I receive a certificate when I finish?
items.answer: Yes. Individual learners receive a SOL Certificate of Completion after finishing all 12 modules and assessments. Team and Enterprise packages include completion certificate templates your organisation can issue to staff under its own branding. This is a completion certificate, not a nationally accredited qualification, unless delivered by an authorised RTO within its own scope.

items.question: Can we white-label the content for our RTO or organisation?
items.answer: Yes. The Team package includes co-branded materials with your organisation's logo and details. The Enterprise / RTO package includes full white-label rights, so all workbooks, slide decks, video scripts and assessments are delivered under your brand with no SOL branding, plus LMS integration support.

items.question: What format are the training materials in?
items.answer: Materials are supplied as editable Word documents, PowerPoint slide decks (.pptx), PDF workbooks and plain-text video scripts. The 1,500+ question quiz bank comes in a structured format that works with most LMS platforms, including Moodle, TalentLMS and LearnDash.

items.question: How quickly do I get access after payment?
items.answer: Individual and Team package materials are emailed to you within 1 business day of payment confirmation. Enterprise packages start with a short onboarding call to apply your branding, with delivery typically within 3–5 business days.

items.question: Can I add modules or get curriculum updates later?
items.answer: Every package includes curriculum updates at no extra cost for the length of your access period. Custom modules for a specific disability support type or workflow can be scoped within the Enterprise package or as an add-on.

items.question: Is live support or mentoring available?
items.answer: The Team package includes 2 live Q&A sessions with a SOL trainer. The Enterprise package includes a train-the-trainer program and unlimited email support during the initial rollout. Individual learners have email support throughout their 6-month access period.

items.question: Can I get a tax invoice or pay by EFT?
items.answer: Yes, we can issue a formal tax invoice for any package. To pay by EFT (bank transfer) instead of online, choose the Enterprise / Custom option in the intake form or email info@solbusinessconsultant.com.au and we will arrange it.

items.question: Which NDIS registration package is right for my organisation?
items.answer: Your audit pathway (verification or certification) depends on the NDIS registration groups you apply for. Most verification-only (Tier 1) providers choose START. If you deliver direct supports (Tier 2) or SIL/SDA (Tier 3), you will likely need CERTIFIED or COMPLETE. Book a free consultation and we will confirm the right fit.

items.question: What is the difference between a verification and a certification audit?
items.answer: Verification audits are simpler and faster (6-8 weeks) and apply to lower-risk services. Certification audits are more comprehensive (10-14 weeks), apply to direct support providers and need more detailed evidence. The NDIS Commission decides which applies based on your registration groups.

items.question: Can I upgrade my package part-way through?
items.answer: Yes. If you start with START and find you need more support, you can upgrade to CERTIFIED or COMPLETE. You simply pay the difference and we provide the extra documentation and support.

items.question: Does the price include ongoing compliance after registration?
items.answer: The COMPLETE package includes 12 months of compliance platform access. START and CERTIFIED cover the registration process only. After registration, optional ongoing support (annual reviews, policy updates and training) is available at hourly rates.

items.question: What happens if the auditor finds non-compliances?
items.answer: Every package includes remediation guidance if the auditor raises non-compliances. Support beyond the included scope is available at hourly rates. Our goal is your successful registration, and we work with you through any findings.

items.question: Do you guarantee NDIS registration approval?
items.answer: No one can guarantee NDIS Commission approval, as that decision rests with the Commission. We make sure your documentation is audit-ready and aligned with the NDIS Practice Standards, and our process has consistently supported organisations through successful registration.

posts.title: Top 5 Bookkeeping Mistakes Small Businesses Make
posts.excerpt: Avoid the bookkeeping mistakes that lead to BAS stress, ATO penalties, compliance problems and cash flow shortfalls in your Australian small business.
posts.content:
Many small businesses fall behind because receipts, bank feeds, payroll records and GST coding are only dealt with when the BAS is due. By then, missing documents and miscoded transactions are harder and more expensive to fix.

Reconciling every month, using clear account categories and saving source documents as you go makes tax time far less stressful, and means management decisions are based on real, up-to-date numbers.

A steady bookkeeping routine in Xero, MYOB or QuickBooks also helps you spot late-paying customers, cash flow pressure and missing records before they turn into costly problems.
